intent: Establish empirically, before writing tests for 565 .sh files, whether Phase 3's constraints are jointly satisfiable: a repo-wide gate at 100% line coverage over ALL shell files, with no suppressions. Phase 1 measured effecting code at 0% under PATH shims; if that were the ceiling, 100% would require either forbidden suppressions or source seams in 17+46 files.
scope: Measurement only - no production file was modified
Subjects: setup_night_lockdown.sh (entry script, 127 lines) and pacman_wrapper.sh (215 lines)
Non-goal: writing the test suites themselves; this answers the feasibility question that gates them
changes: Added this evidence artifact recording the feasibility result

verification.command: jail_run.sh on pacman_wrapper.sh with /usr/local/bin bind-mounted, vs the same cases without that mount
verification.result: pass - generalises, and exposes the dominant failure mode
verification.evidence: 28.95% (22/76) with /usr/local/bin masked vs 75.00% (57/76) without it. The wrapper sources sibling libs from /usr/local/bin and takes its 'libraries missing -> exec pacman unwrapped' escape hatch at lines 44-45 when they vanish, exiting before any real work.

risks: DECISIVE FINDING: 100% line coverage on an entry script is achievable with NO source changes and NO suppressions, so the earlier estimate that 17 files need path seams and 46 need require_root seams is superseded.

--map-root-user ALONE is insufficient for /etc writes: CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE inside a userns only covers files whose owner uid is mapped in. The bind-mount over the write target is what makes the write land.

The jail must supply its own /etc/passwd, /etc/group and /etc/nsswitch.conf. Inside the userns the invoking user does not resolve, so `id -u <user>` fails and aborts any script using it under set -e. This cost three iterations to find.
Entry scripts cannot be staged into a temp dir the way libs can: they resolve libs via BASH_SOURCE and common.sh via `readlink -f "$0"`, so they must be executed in place as $0.

The jail must be PER-SCRIPT: mount only what a script WRITES and preserve what it READS. A blanket jail masking /usr/local/bin cut pacman_wrapper.sh from 75.00% to 28.95%. An over-aggressive mount looks exactly like unreachable code, which is the same misdiagnosis class that produced the false 81.58% ceiling.
Arbitrary argument sets do not drive coverage; cases must be designed from each script's own dispatch logic. This, not the jail, is the dominant per-file cost across 565 files.
Running installers for real as uid 0 inside a namespace is safe only while every write target is mounted; a missing mount plus a writable real path would modify the live system.
